column3: “On the Sabbaths” is rendered “on the Sabbath.”
NASB follows the critical text (“they ate”); “loaves of the presentation” is rendered “consecrated bread.”
NASB follows the critical text with the neuter “something greater.”
NASB renders “mercy” as “compassion” and “the guiltless” as “the innocent.”
Close to the Greek; NASB has no “also,” like the critical text.
NASB adds “there” and “whose,” names “Jesus,” and omits “behold.”
NASB renders the question “How much …?” as an exclamation.
NASB follows the critical text with “many” (without “crowds”).
“Make Him known” is rendered “tell who He was.”
NASB italicizes the supplied “is” and renders “has found delight” as “is well-pleased.”
NASB follows the critical text (“the mute man spoke and saw”); it names “Jesus.”
NASB renders the question “surely not … ?” as “cannot be …, can he?”
NASB names “Jesus,” a Textus Receptus word; “brought to desolation” is “laid waste.”
NASB renders “plunder” as “carry off” and “rob” as “plunder.”
